title: Intelligent retry profiles + request fingerprinting and retriable-signal mapping
creator: Ava Chen
description: Design and implement cross-language SDK primitives that choose conservative, sensible retry/backoff defaults by default while exposing explicit profiles for latency-sensitive, cost-sensitive, and throughput-sensitive workloads. Introduce a lightweight request fingerprinting scheme and idempotency affordances to reduce duplicate side-effects, and publish a retriable-error signal mapping that SDKs can use to classify and surface retriable vs non-retriable failures. Deliver examples and docs for Python/TypeScript/Go and a short migration guide for existing clients.
tasks: Draft retry profile matrix (default, aggressive, conservative, streaming-resume) and map to backoff parameters
Define request fingerprint format and where SDKs will set it (header x-rw-req-fp / generated client-side UUID + deterministic hash)
Create retriable-error taxonomy (transport, transient 5xx, capacity errors, rate-limit with Retry-After semantics, stream disconnects) and canonical codes/messages
Prototype Python SDK implementation of retry profiles and fingerprint header
Prototype TS SDK with abort-signal and streaming resume hooks
Prototype Go SDK with context-aware backoff and id-key wiring
Add telemetry events for retry attempts, dedupe hits, fingerprint collisions, and final outcome
Write examples for common patterns (idempotent generate, non-idempotent fine-tune, resumable streaming chat)
Publish docs + migration guide and deprecation plan for legacy retry options
Add e2e tests that assert no double-execution for idempotent endpoints under simulated flaky network
decisions: Default profile will favor safety: bounded retries (max 3), exponential backoff with capped jitter, and no automatic retries for non-idempotent write-like endpoints
Idempotency affordance: SDKs will offer an explicit idempotency_key parameter and will also generate a client_fingerprint header for observability when user does not provide a key
Fingerprint format: base64url of SHA256(request-method + path + sorted-body-hash-snippets) truncated to 18 bytes to limit header size
Streaming resume: SDKs expose a resume_token produced by server; default streaming profile will not retry entire stream by default but will attempt a single resume request when token present
Retryable classification: rely on server-provided error metadata when available (retryable: true, retry_after), else use client-side heuristics for 5xx and network timeouts
tradeoffs: Generating fingerprints client-side improves dedupe telemetry but increases SDK work and header size; we limit length and make it opt-out
Conservative default reduces accidental duplicates but may surface more client-visible errors for transient backend failures (trade reliability for safety)
Streaming resume complexity: adding resume tokens improves UX for long-lived streams but requires server/contract support and additional test surface
acceptance_criteria: SDKs (py/ts/go) expose a standard RetryProfile enum and honor default conservative profile out-of-the-box
SDKs attach x-rw-req-fp header (or user-provided idempotency_key) to applicable requests
Retryable-error mapping doc published and linked in SDK repos; SDKs consult server signals when available
Automated tests demonstrate that idempotent endpoints do not create duplicate side-effects under simulated retries
Telemetry hooks emit retry_attempt and dedupe_hit events; sample dashboards added to Console
Migration doc and short deprecation timeline published for legacy retry flags
